argument: 1892 fieldwork is best tested as a distributed reference/conversion system, not as an itinerary-discovery project.
baseline: Rossi-Wilcox 2007 already provides a substantial itinerary and uses the 1892 letters.

events.claim: Fieldwork was attached to the commission's financial and shipping system before departure.
Harvard display was part of the fieldwork feedback loop, not merely the terminal destination of finished models.
The expedition was an adaptive production program with delegated preservation labor.
Observation depended on a temporary workstation plus parallel conversion of plants into drawings and preserved reference materials.
The trip produced a mixed reference archive rather than a single medium.
Field observation extended into cultivation, mailed material, photography and institutional garden study.
The route was institutionally coordinated and communication-dependent.
A single passage exposes labor division, specimen conversion, procurement, transport and the microeconomics of fieldwork.
Local botanists converted a passing visit into a procurement node.
Color and ecological setting were recorded under time pressure at a daily production cadence.
Phenology, not geographic completeness, governed route value.
The trip deliberately built a supplier network designed to outlast Rudolf's physical presence.
A botanic garden could substitute for distant field travel by concentrating identified living material and saving time.
Seed procurement compensated for temporal mismatch between the travel calendar and plant life cycles.
The field season closed by folding procurement and maintenance back into observation.
The strongest evidence that the expedition engineered future access rather than merely harvesting a finite set of observations.

guards: Do not claim discovery of the itinerary.
Keep Rudolf's 106 species and the institutional 116 colored drawings as separate counts until reconciled.
Archive-retained ephemera are not proof of physical presence.
Verify OCR and translations against images before quotation.
Do not equate observed plants, preserved specimens, propagules and later models without a specific crosswalk.
next: Crosswalk named plants from letters to drawings, herbarium specimens, model/section labels and later models.
Build a finance/logistics ledger from passage, travel/hotel funding, supply purchases, receipts and shipping.
Resolve dated supplier-network edges for Cameron, Ganong, Orcutt, Parrish, Gillett and botanical-garden staff.
Tag route changes caused by flowering stage, seed season, weather, fatigue and garden substitution.
